101.subject: Botany
options: bacteria whose DNA is relaxed or supercoiled but which have a cytoskeleton as well as mitochondria
bacteria that contain a cytoskeleton and ribosomes and endoplasmic reticulum
archaebacteria that contain protein homologous to eukaryotic core histones
archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is supercoiled.
101.sol: Thermococcus, Methanococcus and Methanobacterium exemplify archaebacteria that lack any histones resembling those found in eukaryotes but whose DNA is negatively supercoiled. Archaebacteria do not have a nucleus, the genetic material floats freely in the cytoplasm. They consist of ribosomal RNA. DNA contains a single, circular molecule, which is compact and tightly wound. No protein is associated with DNA. The archaebacterial cell may contain plasmids, which are small, circular pieces of DNA and have a highly negatively supercoiled DNA.

176.subject: Botany
176.sol: A characteristic of most plant cells is the presence of cytoplasmic material that establish continuity between adjacent cells. These bridges are called plasmodesmata. These permit the free circulation of fluid, which is essential to the maintenance of plant cell toxicity.

1028.text: The density of a gas $A$ is thrice that of a gas $B$ at the same temperature. The molecular weight of gas $B$ is twice that of $A$. What will be the ratio of the pressures acting on $B$ and $A$ ?
1028.sol:
$\frac{d}{p}=\frac{M}{R T}$
Let density of gas $B$ be $d$.
$\therefore \quad$ density of gas A=3 d$ and let molecular weight of A$ be $M$.
$\therefore$ molecular weight of $B=2 M$
Since, $R$ is gas constant and $T$ is same for both gases, so
$\begin{aligned} & p_A=\frac{d_A R T}{M_A} \text{ and } p_B=\frac{d_B R T}{M_B} \\ & \frac{p_B}{p_A}=\frac{d_B}{d_A} \times \frac{M_A}{M_B}=\frac{d}{3 d} \times \frac{M}{2 M}=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}$

2842.text: A covalent molecule $X - Y$ is found to have a dipole moment of $1. 5 \times {10}^{- 29}C. m$ and $a$ bond length of $150$ pm. The percent ionic character of the bond will be
2842.sol:
Dipole moment=& $q \times d$

Bond length $d = 150pm = 150 \times {10}^{- 12}m$

Charge $q = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}$

Dipole moment = $150 \times {10}^{- 12} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} = 2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 29}$

Percentage ionic character =$\dfrac{Dipoleobserved}{Dipolecalculated} \times 100$

Dipole observed =& $1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 29}$

Percentage ionic character = $\dfrac{1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 29}}{2 . 4 \times {10}^{- 29}} \times 100 = 62 . 5$

Hence, the percent ionic character of the bond will be $62 . 5 %$.

4307.subject: Chemistry
4307.text: Which of the following conclusions could not be derived from Rutherford's $\alpha$-particle& scattering experiment:
options: Most of the space in the atom is empty.
The radius of the atom is about ${10}^{- 10}m$, while that of the nucleus is ${10}^{- 15}m$.
Electrons move in circular paths of fixed energy, called orbits.
Electrons and the nucleus are held together by electrostatic forces of attraction.
4307.sol:
Rutherford's scattering experiment established the idea of a nucleus, while& maintaining& that the electrons do not reside in the nucleus.

On the basis of his experiment,& Rutherford put forward the model of an atom& which had the following features:

There is a positively charged centre in an atom called the nucleus. Nearly all the mass of an atom resides in the nucleus.

The size of the nucleus is very small as compared to the size of the atom.

However, Rutherford later suggested that the electrons are revolving in circular orbits.

6202.text: The slope of the normal to the curve $y=\frac{x}{x^2+1}$ at $x=-4$ is
6202.sol:
Slope of normal $=-\left(\frac{d x}{d y}\right)_{\left(x_1, y_1\right)}$
Given curve, $y=\frac{x}{1+x^2}$, then $\begin{aligned}\frac{d y}{d x}$& =$\frac{\left(1+x^2\right)-x(2 x)}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2}=\frac{1-x^2}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2}$\\
\Rightarrow \quad-$\frac{d x}{d y}$& =-$\frac{\left(1+x^2\right)^2}{1-x^2}=\frac{\left(1+x^2\right)^2}{x^2-1}
\end{aligned}$ At $x=-4 \begin{aligned}\left(-\frac{d x}{d y}\right)_{x=-4}$& =$\frac{\left((-4)^2+1\right)^2}{(-4)^2-1}$\\
& =$\frac{(16+1)^2}{16-1}=\frac{17^2}{15}=\frac{289}{15}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Slope of normal to curve $y=\frac{x}{x^2+1}$, at $x=-4$
is $289 / 15$.

6361.text: If $x$ is real, then the minimum value of $\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}$, is
6361.sol: On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get $f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{\left(x^2+x+1\right)(2 x-1)-\left(x^2-x+1\right)(2 x+1)}{\left(x^2+x+1\right)^2}$ for maximum or minimum, put $f^{\prime}(x)=0\begin{array}{lc} \Rightarrow & \left(x^2+x+1\right)(2 x-1)-\left(x^2-x+1\right)(2 x+1)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & x^2+x-1-\left(-x^2+x+1\right)=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 x^2-2=0 \Rightarrow x= \pm 1 \end{array}$ Now, $f^{\prime}(c)=\frac{2 x^2-2}{\left(x^2+x+1\right)^2}$ Again differentiating, we get $\begin{aligned} & \left(x^2+x+1\right)^2(4 x)-\left(2 x^2-2\right) \\ & f^{\prime \prime}(x)=\frac{2\left(x^2+x+1\right)(2 x+1)}{\left(x^2+x+1\right)^4} \end{aligned}$ at $x=1, f^{\prime \prime}(x) > 0$ Therefore it is minimum at $x=1$ Put $x=1$ in equation (i), we get $f(1)=\frac{1-1+1}{1+1+1}=\frac{1}{3}\therefore$ The minimum value is $\frac{1}{3}$.

12460.sol:
We can conclude, the normal& to the plane ${S}_{1}$

i.e. $x - 2y + 2z + 3 = 0$ is& (say) $\overset{→}{r1} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$
and the normal to the plane ${S}_{2}$

i.e. $3x - 2y + 4z - 4 = 0$ is (say) $\overset{→}{r2} = 3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$
So, the normal to the plane ${S}_{3}$ (which is perpendicular to the plane ${S}_{1} and {S}_{2}$)

is $\overset{→}{r3} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 2 \\ 3 & - 2 & 4\end{cases}\right| = - 4\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

So, the equation of plane ${S}_{3}$ is

$- 4x + 2y + 4z + c = 0... \left(1\right)$

As, it is passing through the point $\left(2, 1, 3\right)$

So, substituting in equation $\left(1\right)$, we get,

$- 4 \times2 + 2 \times1 + 4 \times3 + c = 0 ⇒ - 8 + 2 + 12 + c = 0 ⇒ c = - 6$

Hence, the equation of the plane ${S}_{3}$ is

$- 4x + 2y + 4z - 6 = 0 or 2x - y - 2z + 3 = 0$

$= \sqrt{4ax-x^2} + \dfrac{x(2a-x)}{\sqrt{4ax-x^2}} = \dfrac{(4ax-x^2) + x(2a-x)}{\sqrt{4ax-x^2}} = \dfrac{6ax-2x^2}{\sqrt{4ax-x^2}}$

At $x = 2a$:

Since $a > 0$, $f'(2a) = 2a > 0$, so $f(x)$ is increasing at $x = 2a$.

21683.subject: Mathematics
21683.text:
Given $Z=80 x+120 y$, subject to constraints are $x+3 y \leq 30 ; 3 x+4 y \leq 60 ; x \geq 0 ; y \geq 0$.
P is one of the corner points of the feasible region for the given Linear Programming Problem.
Then the coordinate of P is
21683.sol:
The constraints are $x + 3y \leq 30$, $3x + 4y \leq 60$, $x \geq 0$, and $y \geq 0$.

First, identify the intersection points of the boundary lines with the axes:
For $x + 3y = 30$:
If $x = 0$, $y = 10$. Point is $(0,10)$.
If $y = 0$, $x = 30$. Point is $(30,0)$.

For $3x + 4y = 60$:
If $x = 0$, $y = 15$. Point is $(0,15)$.
If $y = 0$, $x = 20$. Point is $(20,0)$.

Next, find the intersection of the two lines $x + 3y = 30$ and $3x + 4y = 60$.
Multiply the first equation by 3: $3x + 9y = 90$.
Subtract the second equation from this: $(3x + 9y) - (3x + 4y) = 90 - 60$, which gives $5y = 30$, so $y = 6$.
Substitute $y = 6$ into $x + 3y = 30$: $x + 3(6) = 30 \Rightarrow x + 18 = 30 \Rightarrow x = 12$.
The intersection point is $(12,6)$.

The feasible region is bounded by the vertices $(0,0)$, $(20,0)$, $(12,6)$, and $(0,10)$.
Comparing these vertices with the given options, $(20,0)$ is a valid corner point.

Answer: $(20,0)$

22102.subject: Mathematics
22102.text: The inclination of a straight line passing through the point $(-3,6)$ and the midpoint of the line joining the points $(4,-5)$ and $(-2,9)$ is
22102.sol:
Let the given points be $A = (4, -5)$ and $B = (-2, 9)$. The midpoint $M$ of the line segment $AB$ is calculated as:

$M = \left( \dfrac{4 + (-2)}{2}, \dfrac{-5 + 9}{2} \right) = \left( \dfrac{2}{2}, \dfrac{4}{2} \right) = (1, 2)$

The line passes through the point $P = (-3, 6)$ and $M = (1, 2)$. The slope $m$ of this line is given by:

$m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \dfrac{2 - 6}{1 - (-3)} = \dfrac{-4}{1 + 3} = \dfrac{-4}{4} = -1$

The inclination $\theta$ of the line is the angle such that $\tan \theta = m$. Thus, $\tan \theta = -1$.

Since $\tan \theta = -1$, the principal value of $\theta$ in the interval $[0, \pi)$ is $\theta = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3 \pi}{4}$

22135.subject: Mathematics
22135.text: The slope of lines which makes an angle $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the line $2 x-y=-7$
22135.sol:
The given line is $2x - y = -7$, which can be written as $y = 2x + 7$. The slope of this line is $m_1 = 2$.

Let the slope of the required line be $m$. The angle $\theta$ between the two lines is $45^{{}^{\circ}}$. Using the formula for the angle between two lines, $\tan \theta = \left| \dfrac{m - m_1}{1 + m m_1} \right|$, we have:

$\tan 45^{{}^{\circ}} = \left| \dfrac{m - 2}{1 + 2m} \right|$

$1 = \left| \dfrac{m - 2}{1 + 2m} \right|$

This gives two cases:

Case 1: $\dfrac{m - 2}{1 + 2m} = 1 \Rightarrow m - 2 = 1 + 2m \Rightarrow m = -3$.

Case 2: $\dfrac{m - 2}{1 + 2m} = -1 \Rightarrow m - 2 = -1 - 2m \Rightarrow 3m = 1 \Rightarrow m = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Thus, the slopes are $-3$ and $\dfrac{1}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3},-3$

22489.subject: Physics
22489.text: A parallel plate capacitor is filled by a dielectric whose relative permittivity varies with the applied voltage (U) as $\epsilon=2 U$. A similar capacitor with no dielectric is charged to $U_0=78 \mathrm{ V}$. It is then connected to the uncharged capacitor with the dielectric. Find the final voltage on the capacitors.
22489.sol:
Let $C_0$ be the capacitance of the capacitor without the dielectric. The charge on this capacitor is $Q_0 = C_0 U_0$, where $U_0 = 78$ V.

When the two capacitors are connected in parallel, the total charge $Q_0$ is shared between them. Let $U$ be the final common voltage. The charge on the first capacitor is $Q_1 = C_0 U$.

The second capacitor has a dielectric with relative permittivity $\epsilon = 2U$. The capacitance of this capacitor is $C = \epsilon C_0 = (2U) C_0$. The charge on this capacitor is $Q_2 = C U = (2U) C_0 U = 2 C_0 U^2$.

By the principle of conservation of charge, $Q_0 = Q_1 + Q_2$.

$C_0 U_0 = C_0 U + 2 C_0 U^2$.

Dividing by $C_0$, we get $U_0 = U + 2U^2$.

Substituting $U_0 = 78$, we have $2U^2 + U - 78 = 0$.

Solving the quadratic equation for $U$ using the quadratic formula $U = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$:

$U = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(2)(-78)}}{2(2)} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 624}}{4} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{625}}{4} = \dfrac{-1 \pm 25}{4}$.

Since voltage must be positive, $U = \dfrac{24}{4} = 6$ V.

Answer: 6V

22615.subject: Physics
22615.text: The SI unit of electrical conductivity is :
22615.sol:
Electrical conductivity, denoted by $\kappa$ or $\sigma$, is defined as the reciprocal of electrical resistivity, $\rho$.

The SI unit of resistivity $\rho$ is $\Omega \cdot \text{m}$.

Therefore, the SI unit of conductivity $\sigma = \dfrac{1}{\rho}$ is $\dfrac{1}{\Omega \cdot \text{m}} = \Omega^{-1} \cdot \textm^{-1}$.

Since the SI unit of conductance $\Omega^{-1}$ is Siemens (S), the unit of conductivity is $\text{S} \cdot \textm^{-1}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{S} \mathrm{ m}^{-1}$

22768.subject: Physics
22768.text: What feature of the infrared waves make it useful for the haze photography?
options: Since it has large wave length
Since it is absorbed by the medium
22768.sol:
Infrared waves have longer wavelengths compared to visible light waves.

According to Rayleigh scattering, the intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength, expressed as $I \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda^{4}}$.

Because infrared waves have larger wavelengths, they undergo significantly less scattering by atmospheric particles such as dust, smoke, and haze compared to visible light.

This reduced scattering allows infrared radiation to penetrate through haze more effectively, making it useful for haze photography.

Answer: Since it has large wave length

23012.subject: Physics
23012.text: In a particular case $X$, a certain length of insulated copper wire is bent to form double loops of equal radii. In another case Y the same copper wire is bent to form three loops of equal radii. If the same steady current is passed through the copper wire in both the cases, the ratio of magnetic field at the centre in the case X to that in case Y is:
23012.sol:
Let $L$ be the total length of the wire. In case $X$, the wire is bent into $n_1 = 2$ loops of radius $r_1$. The circumference of these loops is $2 \times (2 \pi r_1) = L$, so $r_1 = \dfrac{L}{4 \pi}$.

The magnetic field at the center of $n_1$ loops is $B_X = n_1 \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 r_1} = 2 \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 (L / 4 \pi)} = \dfrac{4 \pi \mu_0 I}{L}$.

In case $Y$, the wire is bent into $n_2 = 3$ loops of radius $r_2$. The circumference of these loops is $3 \times (2 \pi r_2) = L$, so $r_2 = \dfrac{L}{6 \pi}$.

The magnetic field at the center of $n_2$ loops is $B_Y = n_2 \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 r_2} = 3 \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 (L / 6 \pi)} = \dfrac{9 \pi \mu_0 I}{L}$.

The ratio of the magnetic fields is $\dfrac{B_X}{B_Y} = \dfrac{4 \pi \mu_0 I / L}{9 \pi \mu_0 I / L} = \dfrac{4}{9}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{9}$

23139.subject: Physics
23139.text: Modulus of rigidity of an incompressible liquid is
23139.sol:
The modulus of rigidity, also known as the shear modulus (G$), is defined as the ratio of shear stress to shear strain. For a fluid, shear stress is proportional to the rate of shear strain, not the shear strain itself. When a static shear force is applied to a liquid, it continues to deform indefinitely as long as the force is applied, meaning the shear strain is not defined for a static state. Consequently, the resistance to shear deformation in a liquid is zero. Therefore, the modulus of rigidity for any liquid, including an incompressible one, is zero.

Answer: Zero$

23140.text: What is the relation obeyed by the angles of contact $\theta_1, \theta_2$ and $\theta_3$ of 3 liquids of different densities $P_1, P_2$ and $P_3$ respectively $(\mathrm{P}_1 < \mathrm{P}_2 < \mathrm{P}_3$) when they rise to the same capillary height in 3 identical capillaries and having nearly same surface tension $\mathrm{T}$ ?

From Jurin's law: $h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{rPg}$

Given $P_1 \lt P_2 \lt P_3$:

$\cos\theta_1 \lt \cos\theta_2 \lt \cos\theta_3$

Since liquids rise ($h \gt 0$), $\cos\theta \gt 0$, so all angles are acute: $0 \leq \theta \lt \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

In $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, cosine is decreasing, so smaller cosine means larger angle:

$\theta_1 \gt \theta_2 \gt \theta_3$

Combined: $\dfrac{\pi}{2} \gt \theta_1 \gt \theta_2 \gt \theta_3 \geq 0$

23343.subject: Physics
23343.text: What is the refractive index of a material of prism if the frequency of light wave in it is $3 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{ Hz}$. The wavelength of light in the material of prism is $8000 Å$.
23343.sol:
The speed of light in a medium is given by the product of its frequency and wavelength. Let $v$ be the speed of light in the material, $f$ be the frequency, and $\lambda$ be the wavelength.

$v = f \times \lambda$

Given $f = 3 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ and $\lambda = 8000 \text{ Å} = 8000 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m} = 8 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.

$v = (3 \times 10^{14}) \times (8 \times 10^{-7}) = 24 \times 10^{7} \text{ m/s} = 2.4 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$.

The refractive index $n$ is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum $c$ to the speed of light in the medium $v$. Taking $c = 3 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$:

$n = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{8}}{2.4 \times 10^{8}} = \dfrac{3}{2.4} = \dfrac{30}{24} = \dfrac{5}{4} = 1.25$.

Answer: 1.25

26591.subject: Physics
26591.text:
At time $t = 0$, a disk of radius $1m$ starts to roll without slipping on a horizontal plane with an angular acceleration of $\alpha = \dfrac{2}{3}rad{s}^{- 2}$. A small stone is stuck to the disk. At $t = 0$, it is at the contact point of the disk and the plane. Later, at time $t = \sqrt{\pi}s$, the stone detaches itself and flies off tangentially from the disk. The maximum height (in $m$) reached by the stone measured from the plane is $\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{x}{10}$. The value of $x$ is [Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$.]

If the numerical value has more than two decimal places, truncate/round-off the value to TWO decimal places.
26591.sol:
Using second equation of motion,

The angle rotated by disc in $t = \sqrt{\pi}s$ is $\theta = {\omega}_{0}t + \dfrac{1}{2}\alpha{t}^{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{3}{\left(\sqrt{\pi}\right)}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{3}rad$

Now using first equation of motion, the angular velocity of disc is $\omega = {\omega}_{0} + \alphat$

$⇒ \omega = 0 + \dfrac{2\sqrt{\pi}}{3} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{\pi}}{3}rad{s}^{- 1}$

And, velocity of disk about centre of mass is ${v}_{cm} = \omegaR = \dfrac{2\sqrt{\pi}}{3} \times 1$

$= \dfrac{2\sqrt{\pi}}{3}m{s}^{- 1}$

At the moment the stone detaches, the situation is shown in figure below.

$v = \sqrt{{\left(\omegaR\right)}^{2} + {v}_{cm}^{2} + 2\left(\omegaR\right){v}_{cm}cos120 °}$

Putting the values, we get

$v = \dfrac{2\sqrt{\pi}}{3}m{s}^{- 1}$

And $tan\theta = \dfrac{\omegaRsin120 °}{{v}_{cm} + \omegaRcos120 °}$

$⇒ tan\theta = \sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}rad$

So, the maximum height reached by the stone is ${H}_{max} = \dfrac{{v}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$

$= \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{\pi}}{3}\right)}^{2} \times \sin^{2}60 °}{2 \times 10}$

$= \dfrac{4\pi \times 3}{9 \times 2 \times 10 \times 4}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{60}m$

So, height from ground will be

$R\left(1 - cos60 °\right) + \dfrac{\pi}{60} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{x}{10}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{6} = 0 . 52$

29105.subject: Chemistry
29105.text: Alkaline oxidative fusion of ${MnO}_{2}$ gives "$A$ " which on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline solution produces $B . A$and $B$ respectively are:
29105.sol:
The alkaline oxidative fusion is a redox reaction (undergoes both oxidation and reduction simultaneously) in which a compound undergoes fusion with itself only, in the presence of a base or an alkaline solution. 

Electrolysis is a chemical process where an electric current is passed through an electrolyte, causing a non-spontaneous chemical reaction to occur, typically resulting in the decomposition of the electrolyte into its constituent elements or ions.

Alkaline oxidative fusion of ${MnO}_{2}$ :
$2{MnO}_{2} + 4{OH}^{-} + {O}_{2} \to 2{MnO}_{4}^{2 -} + 2{H}_{2}O$

Electrolytic oxidation of ${MnO}_{4}^{2 -}$ in alkaline medium.
${MnO}_{4}^{2 -} \to {MnO}_{4}^{-} + {e}^{-}$

Hence, the answer is option B.

29553.text: Some gases are responsible for heating of atmosphere (green house effect). Identify from the following the gaseous species which does not cause it.

In Duma's method of estimation of nitrogen, $0 . 1840g$ of an organic compound gave $30mL$ of nitrogen collected at $287K$ and $758mm$ of $Hg$ pressure. The percentage composition of nitrogen in the compound is ______. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).

In Duma's method of estimation of Nitrogen. $0 . 1840gm$ of organic compound gave $30mL$ of nitrogen which is collected at $287K$ and $758mm$ of $Hg$.

Given ;

Aqueous tension at $287K = 14mm$of $Hg$.

Hence, actual pressure $= \left(758 - 14\right)$

$= 744mm$ of $Hg$.

Volume of nitrogen at $STP = \dfrac{273 \times 744 \times 30}{287 \times 760}$

$V = 27 . 935mL$

$∵ 22400mL$ of ${N}_{2}$ at STP weighs $= 28gm$.

$∴ 27 . 94mL$ of ${N}_{2}$ at $STP$ weighs $= \left(\dfrac{28}{22400} \times 27 . 94\right)gm$

$= 0 . 0349gm$

Hence $%$ of Nitrogen $= \left(\dfrac{0 . 0349}{0 . 1840} \times 100\right)$

$= 18 . 97 %$

Round off. Answer $= 19 %$

30888.subject: Chemistry
30888.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Elements ' $X$ ' and ' $Y$ ' are the most and least electronegative elements, respectively among $\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{As}, \mathrm{Sb}$ and P. The nature of the oxides $\mathrm{X}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{Y}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$ is acidic and amphoteric, respectively.
Statement II : $\quad \mathrm{BCl}_{3}$ is covalent in nature and gets hydrolysed in water. It produces $\left[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}\right]^{-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{B}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ in aqueous medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
30888.sol:
For Statement I:
Among N, As, Sb, P, the electronegativity order is N > P > As > Sb. Thus X = N (most electronegative) and Y = Sb (least electronegative). $N_2O_3$ is acidic (forms HNO₂ with water) and $Sb_2O_3$ is amphoteric (reacts with both acids and bases).
Statement I is true.
For Statement II:
While $BCl_3$ is covalent and hydrolyzes in water to form $B(OH)_3$, the hydrolysis products are incorrect. In neutral aqueous medium, $B(OH)_3$ is formed. The tetrahedral $[B(OH)_4]^-$ forms only in basic conditions, and boron does not form $[B(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ (boron is not a typical transition metal).
Statement II is false.

31652.text:
A substance ' X ' (1.5 g) dissolved in 150 g of a solvent ' Y ' (molar mass $=300 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$) led to an elevation of the boiling point by 0.5 K. The relative lowering in the vapour pressure of the solvent ' Y ' is $\_\_\_\_$ $\times 10^{-2}$. (nearest integer)
[Given : $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}$ of the solvent $=5.0 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ ]
Assume the solution to be dilute and no association or dissociation of $X$ takes place in solution.
31652.sol:
Using boiling point elevation to find molality:
$\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$ gives $0.5 = 5.0 \times m$, so $m = 0.1$ mol/kg.
Converting molality to moles of solute:
$0.1 = \frac{\text{moles of X}}{0.15}$, giving moles of X = 0.015 mol.
Molar mass of X = 1.5 g / 0.015 mol = 100 g/mol.
For vapor pressure lowering, the relative lowering equals the mole fraction of solute.
Moles of solvent Y = 150 g / 300 g/mol = 0.5 mol.
Relative lowering of vapor pressure
= $\frac{n_X}{n_X + n_Y} = \frac{0.015}{0.015 + 0.5}$
$= \frac{0.015}{0.515} = 0.0291 \approx 3 \times 10^{-2}$

35030.text: A ray of light through $\left(2, 1\right)$ is reflected at a point $P$ on the $y -$ axis and then passes through the point $\left(5, 3\right) .$ If this reflected ray is the directrix of an ellipse with eccentricity $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and the distance of the nearer focus from this directrix is $\dfrac{8}{\sqrt{53}},$ then the equation of the other directrix can be:
35030.sol:
The reflected point of $\left(2, 1\right)$ is $\left(- 2, 1\right) .$

Equation of reflected ray

$y - 1 = \dfrac{3 - 1}{5 + 2}\left(x + 2\right)$

$⇒ y - 1 = \dfrac{2}{7}\left(x + 2\right)$

$⇒ 7y - 7 = 2x + 4$

$⇒ 2x - 7y + 11 = 0$

Let the equation of other directrix is

$2x - 7y + \lambda = 0$

Distance of directrix from focus

$\dfrac{a}{e} - ae = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{53}}$, where $e$ is the eccentricity

$⇒ 3a - \dfrac{a}{3} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{53}}$ or $a = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{53}}$

Distance from other focus $\dfrac{a}{e} + ae$

$= 3a + \dfrac{a}{3} = \dfrac{10a}{3} = \dfrac{10}{3} \times \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{53}} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{53}}$

Distance between two directrix $= \dfrac{2a}{e}$

$= 2 \times 3 \times \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{53}} = \dfrac{18}{\sqrt{53}}$

So, $\left|\dfrac{\lambda - 11}{\sqrt{53}}\right| = \dfrac{18}{\sqrt{53}}$

$⇒ \lambda - 11 = 18$ or $- 18$

$⇒ 2x - 7y - 7 = 0$ or $2x - 7y + 29 = 0$

Also given that the common tangent of $H \text{ and } E$ is $y = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}x + k$ $\left(i . e . m = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}\right)$

We know that the condition for common tangent of ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$ and hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{A}^{2}} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{B}^{2}} = 1$ is ${a}^{2}{m}^{2} + {b}^{2} = {A}^{2}{m}^{2} - {B}^{2}$

Now, for common tangency: $\dfrac{5}{2}{a}^{2} + {b}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{2} - 1$

$\dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2{a}^{2}} ⇒ {a}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ {a}^{2} + {b}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ 4\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right) = 3$

36599.text: An urn contains $6$ white and $9$ black balls. Two successive draws of $4$ balls are made without replacement. The probability, that the first draw gives all white balls and the second draw gives all black balls, is :
36599.sol:
Total number of balls in the bag $= 6 + 9 = 15$.

Number of white balls $= 6$.

Number of black balls $= 9$.

Four balls are drawn at random at a time.

The probability that first draw give four white balls

$\dfrac{C4 6}{C4 15} = \dfrac{1}{91}$

The balls are not replaced.

Now, the probability that second draw give four black balls

$\dfrac{C4 9}{C4 11} = \dfrac{21}{55}$

The probability that the first draw give four white balls  and second draw give four black balls

$= \dfrac{1}{91} \times \dfrac{21}{55} = \dfrac{3}{715}$

Hence, the required probability is $\dfrac{3}{715}$.

36976.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of the equation, $x^2-4 \sqrt{2} k x+2 e^{4 \ln k}-1=0$ for some $k$, and $\alpha^2+\beta^2=66$, then $\alpha^3+\beta^3$ is equal to:
36976.sol:
$x^2-4 \sqrt{2} k x+2 e^{4 \ln k}-1=0$ or, $x^2-4 \sqrt{2} k x+2 k^4-1=0 \alpha+\beta=4 \sqrt{2} k$ and $\alpha \cdot \beta=2 k^4-1$ Squaring both sides, we get

\begin{aligned}
&(\alpha+\beta)^2=(4 \sqrt{2} k)^2 \\
&\Rightarrow \alpha^2+\beta^2+2 \alpha \beta=32 k^2 \\
&66+2 \alpha \beta=32 k^2 \\
&66+2 $\left(2 k^4-1\right)$=32 k^2 \\
&66+4 k^4-2=32 k^2 \\
&\Rightarrow 4 k^4-32 k^2+64=0 \\
&$\text{ or, }$ k^4-8 k^2+16=0 \\
&\Rightarrow $\left(k^2\right)^2$-8 k^2+16=0 \\
&\Rightarrow $\left(k^2-4\right)\left(k^2-4\right)=0 \\
&\Rightarrow k^2=4, k^2=4 \\
&\Rightarrow k=\pm 2
\end{aligned}

Now, $\alpha^3+\beta^3=(\alpha+\beta) $\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2-\alpha \beta\right) 
\therefore \alpha^3+\beta^3=(4 \sqrt{2} k) \left[66-\left(2 k^4-1\right)$\right]

Putting $k=-2,(k=+2$ cannot be taken because it does not satisfy the above equation)
$\therefore \alpha^3+\beta^3=(4 \sqrt{2}(-2))\left[66-2(-2)^4-1\right] \alpha^3+\beta^3=(-8 \sqrt{2})(66-32+1)= (-8 \sqrt{2})(35) \therefore \alpha^3+\beta^3=-280 \sqrt{2}$

37113.text: Let ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, \ldots$. be a G.P. of increasing positive numbers. Then $6\left({a}_{2} + {a}_{4}\right)\left({a}_{4} + {a}_{6}\right)$ is equal to
37113.sol:
Given,

${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, \ldots$. be a G.P. of increasing positive numbers,

And the sum of its ${6}^{\text{th}}$ and ${8}^{\text{th}}$ terms be $2$

So, ${a}_{6} + {a}_{8} = 2$

$⇒ a{r}^{5} + a{r}^{7} = 2 . . . . . \left(1\right)$

And the product of its ${3}^{\text{rd}}$ and ${5}^{\text{th}}$ terms be $\dfrac{1}{9}$,

So, ${a}_{3} \cdot {a}_{5} = \dfrac{1}{9} ⇒ {a}^{2} \cdot {r}^{2} \cdot {r}^{4} = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$⇒ a{r}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Now from putting the value of $a{r}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{{r}^{2}}{3} + \dfrac{{r}^{4}}{3} = 2$

$⇒ {r}^{4} + {r}^{2} = 6$

$⇒ \left({r}^{2} + 3\right)\left({r}^{2} - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ {r}^{2} = 2$

$a{r}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{3} ⇒ ar \cdot 2 = \dfrac{1}{3} ⇒ ar = \dfrac{1}{6}$

Now finding the value of $6\left({a}_{2} + {a}_{4}\right)\left({a}_{4} + {a}_{6}\right)$, we get

$= 6\left(ar + a{r}^{3}\right)\left(a{r}^{3} + a{r}^{5}\right)$

$= 6\left(\dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

$= 6 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 1 = 3$

38992.text:
An electron of a hydrogen like atom, having $Z = 4$, jumps from ${4}^{th}$ energy state to ${2}^{nd}$ energy state, The energy released in this process, will be: (Given $Rch = 13 . 6eV$)

Where $R =$ Rydberg

constant $c =$Speed of light in vacuum

$h =$ Planck's constant
38992.sol:
According to Bohr's atomic theory, whenever an electron jumps from one orbit to another, there is always an emission or absorption energy in terms of emission or absorption of photons.

The formula to calculate the energy $\left(∆ E\right)$ of the emitted or absorbed photon when an electron jumps from a state with quantum number ${n}_{1}$ to another with quantum number ${n}_{2}$ is given by

$∆ E = - Rch{Z}^{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{{{n}_{i}}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{{n}_{f}}^{2}}\right] . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

where, $R$ is Rydberg's constant, $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light and $Z$ is the atomic number.

Substitute the values of the given parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required energy.

$\begin{cases}∆ E & = & - 13 . 6 \times {\left(4\right)}^{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{{4}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}}\right]eV \\ = & - 13 . 6 \times 16 \times \left[\dfrac{1}{16} - \dfrac{1}{4}\right]eV \\ = & 40 . 8eV\end{cases}$

39147.text:
A parallel plate capacitor with plate area $A$ and plate separation $d$ is filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant $K = 4 .$ The thickness of the dielectric material is $x,$ where $x < d .$

Let ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ be the capacitance of the system for $x = \dfrac{1}{3}d$ and $x = \dfrac{2d}{3},$ respectively. If ${C}_{1} = 2\mu F$, the value of ${C}_{2}$ is _____ $\mu F .$
39147.sol:
The formula to calculate the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor having thickness $d$ and with a dielectric of thickness $x$ between the plates is given by

$C = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{\left(d - x\right) + \dfrac{x}{K}} . . . ( 1 )$

Substitute the values of the parameters for first case into equation (1) to obtain the capacitance.

$\begin{cases}{C}_{1} & = & \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{\dfrac{2d}{3} + \dfrac{\dfrac{d}{3}}{4}} \\ & = & \dfrac{4{ε}_{0}A}{3d} . . . ( 2 )\end{cases}$

Similarly, substitute the parameters into equation (1) for the second case to obtain the capacitance

$\begin{cases}{C}_{2} & = & \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{\dfrac{d}{3} + \dfrac{\dfrac{2d}{3}}{4}} \\ & = & \dfrac{4{ε}_{0}A}{2d} \\ & = & \dfrac{2{ε}_{0}A}{d} . . . ( 3 )\end{cases}$

Divide equation (3) by equation (2) to obtain the capacitance in the second case.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1}} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{2{ε}_{0}A}{d}}{\dfrac{4{ε}_{0}A}{3d}} \\ & = & \dfrac{3}{2} \\ {C}_{2} & = & \dfrac{3}{2}{C}_{1} . . . ( 4 )\end{cases}$

Substitute the value of the capacitance in the first case into equation (4) to obtain the value of the capacitance in the second case.

$\begin{cases}{C}_{2} & = & \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2\mu F \\ & = & 3\mu F\end{cases}$

39919.subject: Physics
39919.text: The graph shows variation of stopping potential $V_o$ with the frequency $\nu$ of the incident radiation for three photosensitive metals $X_1$, $X_2$ and $X_3$. Which metal will give out electrons with greater kinetic energy, for the same wavelength of incident radiation?
options: All the metals will give out photo electrons with same kinetic energies.
39919.sol:
From Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by:

$K_{ ext{max}} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$

where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of incident radiation and $\Phi$ is the work function of the metal.

The work function is related to the threshold frequency $ u_0$ by $\Phi = h u_0$. From the given graph, the x-intercept represents the threshold frequency. We can observe that:

$ u_0(X_1) < u_0(X_2) < u_0(X_3)$

Therefore, the work functions of the metals follow the order:

$\Phi(X_1) < \Phi(X_2) < \Phi(X_3)$

For the same wavelength $\lambda$ of incident radiation, the term $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$ is constant. Thus, the kinetic energy $K_{ ext{max}}$ will be greatest for the metal with the smallest work function.

Since metal $X_1$ has the minimum work function, it will emit electrons with the greatest kinetic energy.

Answer: $X_1$

40861.text: The time period of a satellite, revolving above earth's surface at a height equal to $R$ will be (Given $g = {\pi}^{2}m{s}^{- 2}, R =$ radius of earth)
40861.sol:
The velocity of the satellite revolving round the Earth at a height $r$ from the centre of the Earth is given by

$v = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{GM}{r}\right)} . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the time period in the circular orbit is given by

$T = \dfrac{2\pir}{v} . . . \left(2\right)$

In this case: $r = R + R = 2R$

Substitute the expression for the velocity from equation (1) into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required time period.

$\begin{cases}T & = & \dfrac{2\pir}{\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}} \\ & = & \dfrac{2\pi \times 2R}{\sqrt{\dfrac{gR}{2}}} \\ & = & \dfrac{4\piR\sqrt{2}}{\pi\sqrt{R}} \\ & = & 4\sqrt{2R} \\ & = & \sqrt{32R}\end{cases}$

43255.text:
A uniform disc with mass $M = 4kg$ and radius $R = 10cm$ is mounted on a fixed horizontal axle as shown in figure. A block with mass $m = 2kg$ hangs from a massless cord that is wrapped around the rim of the disc. During the fall of the block, the cord does not slip and there is no friction at the axle. The tension in the cord is _____ $N$.

(Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
43255.sol:
Let $a$ be the acceleration of block and $\alpha$ be the angular acceleration of disc.

Now, for unwrapping without slipping, $R\alpha = a$.

Forces acting on block are shown in FDB.

Using Newton's second law

$mg - T = ma . . . \left(1\right)$

Torque about centre of disc is $τ = Ia$

$TR = \dfrac{M{R}^{2}}{2}\alpha = \dfrac{4{R}^{2}}{2}\alpha = ⇒ T = 2R\alpha . . . \left(2\right)$

Putting the value of tension in equation $\left(1\right)$, we get

$mg - 2R\alpha = ma ⇒ mg - 2R\dfrac{a}{R} = ma ⇒ mg - 2a = ma ⇒ ma + 2a = mg ⇒ a = \dfrac{mg}{m + 2} = \dfrac{2 \times 10}{2 + 2} = 5m{s}^{- 2}$

Now, $\alpha = \dfrac{5}{0 . 1} = 50rad{s}^{- 2}$

Tension in the cord is $T = 2 \times 0 . 1 \times 50 =$$10N$.

43824.subject: Physics
43824.text:
The internal energy of a monoatomic gas is 3 nRT. One mole of helium is kept in a cylinder having internal cross section area of $17 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$ and fitted with a light movable frictionless piston. The gas is heated slowly by suppling 126 J heat. If the temperature rises by $4^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, then the piston will move $\_\_\_\_$ cm.
(atmospheric pressure $=10^{5} \mathrm{~Pa}$)
43824.sol:
The question states the internal energy of the gas is $U = 3nRT$.
The change in internal energy is $\Delta U = 3nR\Delta T$.
Given: $n = 1$ mole, $\Delta T = 4^{\circ}C = 4$ K, and $R \approx 8.314$ J/mol·K.
$\Delta U = 3 \times 1 \times 8.314 \times 4 = 99.768$ J.
According to the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta Q = \Delta U + W$.
Given heat supplied $\Delta Q = 126$ J.
Work done by the gas $W = \Delta Q - \Delta U = 126 - 99.768 = 26.232$ J.
Since the piston is light and movable, the process occurs at constant atmospheric pressure $P = 10^5$ Pa.
Work done $W = P \Delta V = P(A \times d)$, where $A$ is the cross-section area and $d$ is the displacement of the piston.
$A = 17 \text{ cm}^2 = 17 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$.
$26.232 = 10^5 \times (17 \times 10^{-4}) \times d$.
$26.232 = 170 \times d$.
$d = \frac{26.232}{170} \approx 0.1543$ m.
Converting to cm: $d \approx 15.43$ cm.
Rounding to the nearest option, we get $15.5$ cm.

44002.text: A Carnot engine absorbs $1000 \mathrm{~J}$ of heat energy from a reservoir at $127^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and rejects $600 \mathrm{~J}$ of heat energy during each cycle. The efficiency of engine and temperature of sink will be:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{Q}_2=600 \mathrm{~J} \\
&\mathrm{~T}_1=127^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=400 \mathrm{~K} \\
&\mathrm{~T}_2=? \\
&\eta=?
\end{aligned}
$$
Efficiency of carnot engine,
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\eta=\frac{W}{Q_1} \times 100 \% \\
&\text{ or, } \eta=\frac{Q_2-Q_1}{Q_1} \times 100 \%
\end{aligned}
$$
or, $\eta=\frac{\mathrm{Q}_2-\mathrm{Q}_1}{\mathrm{Q}_1} \times 100 \%$
or, $\eta=\frac{1000-600}{1000} \times 100 \%$
$$
\eta=40 \%
$$
Now, for carnot cycle $\frac{\mathrm{Q}_2}{\mathrm{Q}_1}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_2}{\mathrm{~T}_1}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{600}{1000}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_2}{400} \\
&\mathrm{~T}_2=\frac{600 \times 400}{1000}=240 \mathrm{~K}=240-273 \\
&\therefore \mathrm{T}_2=-33^{\circ} \mathrm{C}
\end{aligned}
$$

$⇒ \alpha{r}^{2} = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{r} ⇒ m{v}^{2} = \alpha{r}^{3}$

$∴$ Kinetic energy $K . E . = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

Also $dU = - \overset{\to}{F} . d\overset{\to}{r}$

$∆ U = - ∫ \overset{\to}{F} . d\overset{\to}{r}$

$= - ∫ \alpha{r}^{2}\left(- dr\right)$

$= \alpha\mathop{∫}_{0}^{r}{r}^{2}dr$

$U - 0 = \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{3}$

$⇒ U = \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{3}$

So total mechanical energy

$E = U + K$

$= \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{3} + \dfrac{\alpha{r}^{3}}{2}$

$E = \dfrac{5\alpha{r}^{3}}{6}$

46507.subject: Physics
46507.text: A mass of Hg is executing SHM which is given by $x=6.0 \cos \left(100 t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \mathrm{cm}$. What is the maximum kinetic energy?
46507.sol:
Here, $\mathrm{m}=1 \mathrm{~kg}$
The given equation of SHM is
$x=6.0 \cos \left(100 t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
Comparing it with equation of SHM,
$\begin{aligned} x & =A \cos (\omega t+\phi), \text{ we have } \\ A & =6.0 \mathrm{~cm}=\frac{6}{100} \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$
and $\quad \omega=100 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
Maximum kinetic energy $=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}\left(\mathrm{v}_{\max }\right)^2$
$=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}(\mathrm{~A} \omega)^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times\left[\frac{6}{100} \times 100\right]^2=18 \mathrm{~J}$

51931.subject: Mathematics
51931.text: The number of ordered pairs $\left(a, b\right)$ of positive integers such that $\dfrac{2a - 1}{b} and \dfrac{2b - 1}{a}$ are both integers is&
51931.sol:
For positive integers '$a$' and '$b$' the numbers $\dfrac{2a - 1}{b} and \dfrac{2b - 1}{a}$ are integers if '$a$' and '$b$' and odd integers because '$2a - 1$' and '$2b - 1$' are odd integers. 

Now, let $\dfrac{2a - 1}{b} = \alpha$ and $\dfrac{2b - 1}{a} = \beta$, where $\alpha, \beta$ are integers.

then $2a - 1 = \alphab$ and $2b - 1 = \betaa$

so $4a - 2 = \alpha \left(\betaa + 1\right)

$⇒ a = $\dfrac{\alpha + 2}{4 - \alpha\beta}

$∵$ $a$ is an integer, then $0 < \alpha\beta < 4$

$∴$ Possible value of $\alpha = 1, 2 or 3 and \beta = 1, 2 or 3$

such that $0 < \alpha\beta < 4$

Now, when \left(\alpha, \beta\right) = \left(1, 1\right), then \left(a, b\right) = \left(1, 1\right)

When \left(\alpha, \beta\right) = \left(1, 2\right), then \left(a, b\right) have no value

When $( \alpha, \beta ) = ( 1, 3 )$, then \left(a, b\right)$ = $\left(3, 5\right)$ and similarly when $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ = $\left(3, 1\right)$, then $\left(a, b\right)$ = $\left(5, 3\right)$ 

So, number of ordered pairs $\left(a, b\right)$ is $3$.

55766.subject: Chemistry
55766.text: What is the total number of electrons present in bonding and antibonding orbitals respectively in $\text{F}_2$ molecule according to MO theory ?
55766.sol:
The atomic number of fluorine ($\text{F}$) is $9$. Therefore, the total number of electrons in the $\text{F}_2$ molecule is $18$.

According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the electronic configuration of $\text{F}_2$ is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}{}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_y}{}^2$

The electrons present in orbitals without an asterisk are bonding electrons ($N_b$), and those in orbitals with an asterisk are antibonding electrons ($N_a$).

Number of bonding electrons ($N_b$) = $2 (\sigma_{1s}) + 2 (\sigma_{2s}) + 2 (\sigma_{2p_z}) + 2 (\pi_{2p_x}) + 2 (\pi_{2p_y}) = 10$

Number of antibonding electrons ($N_a$) = $2 (\sigma^{*}_{1s}) + 2 (\sigma^{*}_{2s}) + 2 (\pi^{*}_{2p_x}) + 2 (\pi^{*}_{2p_y}) = 8$

Thus, there are $10$ bonding electrons and $8$ antibonding electrons.

Answer: Bonding - 10, Antibonding - 8

60239.subject: Mathematics
60239.text: If $x$ and y are sides of two squares such that $\mathrm{y}=x-x^2$, then the rate of change of area of the second square with respect to that of the first square is
60239.sol:
Let $x$ represent the side length of the first square and $y$ the side length of the second. The area of the first square is $A_1 = x^2$, and the area of the second is $A_2 = y^2$.

Given that $y = x - x^2$, we express $A_2$ in terms of $x$ as $A_2 = (x - x^2)^2 = x^2(1 - x)^2 = x^2(1 - 2x + x^2) = x^4 - 2x^3 + x^2$.

The rate of change $\frac{dA_2}{dA_1}$ is found using the chain rule: $\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = \frac{dA_2/dx}{dA_1/dx}$.

Differentiating $A_1 = x^2$ gives $\frac{dA_1}{dx} = 2x$.
Differentiating $A_2 = x^4 - 2x^3 + x^2$ yields $\frac{dA_2}{dx} = 4x^3 - 6x^2 + 2x$.

Substituting these into the chain rule expression:

$\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = \frac{4x^3 - 6x^2 + 2x}{2x}$.

For $x > 0$, factor and simplify:

$\frac{dA_2}{dA_1} = \frac{2x(2x^2 - 3x + 1)}{2x} = 2x^2 - 3x + 1$.

This result corresponds to option C.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

60691.text: If a body cools from $80^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ to $50^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ in the room temperature of $25^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ in 30 minutes, then the temperature of the body after 1 hour is

\Rightarrow & \mathrm{k}=-\frac{1}{30} \log \frac{5}{11} \\

61071.subject: Mathematics
61071.sol:
Consider the integral $I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\mathrm{d}x}{1+(\cot x)^{101}}$.

Applying the substitution $x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2} - x$ yields $I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\mathrm{d}x}{1+(\tan x)^{101}}$.

Adding these two expressions gives $2I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \left( \frac{1}{1+(\cot x)^{101}} + \frac{1}{1+(\tan x)^{101}} \right) \mathrm{d}x$.

The integrand simplifies to $1$ since $\frac{1}{1+(\cot x)^{101}} + \frac{1}{1+(\tan x)^{101}} = \frac{(\tan x)^{101}}{(\tan x)^{101}+1} + \frac{1}{1+(\tan x)^{101}} = 1$.

Therefore, $2I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} 1 \mathrm{d}x = \frac{\pi}{2}$, and $I = \frac{\pi}{4}$.

Final answer: $I = \frac{\pi}{4}$

61096.text: Let $f$ and $g$ be continuous functions on $[0, \mathrm{a}]$ such that $\mathrm{f}(x)=\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{a}-x)$ and $g(x)+g(a-x)=4$, then $\int_0^a f(x) g(x) d x$ is equal to
61096.sol:
$Given,
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{f}(x)=\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}) \\
& \mathrm{g}(x)+\mathrm{g}(\mathrm{a}-x)=4 \\
& \text{ Let } \mathrm{I}=\int_0^{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{f}(x) \mathrm{g}(x) \mathrm{d} x \\
& =\int_0^a f(a-x) \cdot g(a-x) d x \\
& =\int_0^{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{f}(x) \cdot[(4-\mathrm{g}(x)] \mathrm{d} x \\
& =4 \int_0^a \mathrm{f}(x) \mathrm{d} x-\int_0^a \mathrm{f}(x) \mathrm{g}(x) \mathrm{d} x \\
& \mathrm{I}=4 \int_0^{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{f}(x) \mathrm{d} x-\mathrm{I} \\
& 2 \mathrm{I}=4 \int_0^{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{f}(x) \mathrm{d} x \\
& \therefore \quad \mathrm{I}=2 \int_0^{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{f}(x) \mathrm{d} x
\end{aligned}$

62916.subject: Mathematics
62916.text: If $\sim p \vee q$ is false then which of the following is correct?
62916.sol:
Given $\sim p \vee q$ is false.

A disjunction is false only when both of its components are false.

Therefore, $\sim p$ is false and $q$ is false.

This implies $p$ is true (T$) and $q$ is false (F$).

Checking the given options:

$p \leftrightarrow q \equiv T \leftrightarrow F \equiv F$

$p \rightarrow q \equiv T \rightarrow F \equiv F$

$q \rightarrow p \equiv F \rightarrow T \equiv T$

Thus, $q \rightarrow p$ is $T$.

Answer: $q \rightarrow p$ is $T$

62936.subject: Mathematics
62936.text:
If the statements
p: If voltage increases then current decreases.
q : If voltage does not increases then current does not decreases.
r : If current decreases then voltage increases.
s : If current does not decreases then voltage does not increases.
then which of the following pairs of statements having same meaning
62936.sol:
Let $V$ be the statement "voltage increases".

Let $C$ be the statement "current decreases".

The given statements can be represented symbolically as:

$p : V \rightarrow C$

$q : \sim V \rightarrow \sim C$

$r : C \rightarrow V$

$s : \sim C \rightarrow \sim V$

A conditional statement is logically equivalent to its contrapositive (A \rightarrow B \equiv \sim B \rightarrow \sim A$).

The contrapositive of statement $p$ (V \rightarrow C$) is $\sim C \rightarrow \sim V$, which is exactly statement $s$. Thus, $p$ and $s$ are logically equivalent.

The contrapositive of statement $q$ (\sim V \rightarrow \sim C$) is $C \rightarrow V$, which is exactly statement $r$. Thus, $q$ and $r$ are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the pairs of statements having the same meaning are $p, s$ and $q, r$.

Answer: p, s and q, r$

63660.subject: Mathematics
63660.text: In a game, 3 coins are tossed. A person is paid ₹150 if he gets all heads or all tails and he is supposed to pay ₹50 if he gets one head or two heads. The amount he can expect to win / lose on an average per game in ₹ is
63660.sol:
The expected value of the game is calculated using $E = \sum (x_i \cdot P(x_i))$ where $x_i$ represents the payout for each outcome and $P(x_i)$ its probability.

When tossing three coins, the sample space contains $2^3 = 8$ equally likely outcomes.

All heads or all tails occurs in 2 outcomes with probability $\frac{2}{8} = \frac{1}{4}$ and yields ₹150.

Exactly one or two heads occurs in the remaining 6 outcomes with probability $\frac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4}$ and costs ₹50.

The expected value is:
$E = (150 \cdot \frac{1}{4}) + (-50 \cdot \frac{3}{4}) = \frac{150}{4} - \frac{150}{4} = 0$

The expected win/loss amount is ₹0.

64937.subject: Mathematics
64937.text: In $\triangle ABC$, if $\angle C = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, then the value of $\cos^2 A + \cos^2 B + \cos A\cos B$ is...
64937.sol:
Given $A + B + C = \pi$ and $C = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, we have $A + B = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

The given expression is $\cos^2 A + \cos^2 B + \cos A\cos B$.

Using the identity $\cos^2 A + \cos^2 B = 1 + \dfrac{\cos 2A + \cos 2B}{2}$, we get:

$\cos^2 A + \cos^2 B = 1 + \cos(A+B)\cos(A-B)$

Also, using the product-to-sum formula:

$\cos A\cos B = \dfrac{\cos(A+B) + \cos(A-B)}{2}$

Substituting these into the expression, we get:

$1 + \cos(A+B)\cos(A-B) + \dfrac{\cos(A+B) + \cos(A-B)}{2}$

Since $A + B = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, we have $\cos(A+B) = \cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Substituting $\cos(A+B) = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ into the expression:

$1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(A-B) + \dfrac{-\dfrac{1}{2} + \cos(A-B)}{2}$

$= 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(A-B) - \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(A-B)$

$= 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{4}$

67654.subject: Physics
67654.text: A wire carrying current 'I' along x axis has length 'L' and it is kept in a magnetic field $B(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k})$ T. The magnitude of magnetic force acting on the wire is
67654.sol:
The magnetic force on a current-carrying wire is given by $\vec{F} = I(\vec{L} \times \vec{B})$.

Since the wire is along the x-axis, the length vector is $\vec{L} = L\hat{i}$.

The magnetic field is given as $\vec{B} = B(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$.

Substituting these into the force formula:

$\vec{F} = I[L\hat{i} \times B(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})]$

$\vec{F} = ILB[\hat{i} \times \hat{i} + 2(\hat{i} \times \hat{j}) - 2(\hat{i} \times \hat{k})]$

Using the cross product rules $\hat{i} \times \hat{i} = 0$, $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, and $\hat{i} \times \hat{k} = -\hat{j}$:

$\vec{F} = ILB[0 + 2\hat{k} - 2(-\hat{j})] = 2ILB(\hat{j} + \hat{k})$

The magnitude of the magnetic force is:

$|\vec{F}| = \sqrt{(2ILB)^2 + (2ILB)^2} = \sqrt{8I^2L^2B^2} = \sqrt{8}ILB$

Answer: $\sqrt{8}\,\text{ILB}$

67679.subject: Physics
67679.text:
An infinitely long straight conductor carrying current ' $I$ ' is bent into a shape as shown in figure. The radius of the circular loop is ' $r$ '. The magnetic induction at the centre of the loop at point ' $o$ ' is
$\text{ ( } \mu_0=\text{ permeability$ of free space) }
67679.sol:
Magnetic induction at the center of the loop is found by superposition of contributions from the semicircular arc and both straight conductors.

The semicircular loop of radius $r$ with clockwise current $I$ contributes a field directed into the page. For a semicircular arc, the field magnitude is half that of a full loop: $B_{\text{loop}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4r}$.

The two semi-infinite straight conductors, each carrying current $I$ to the right, are at perpendicular distance $r$ from the center. Each contributes a field directed out of the page with magnitude $\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$, giving a combined contribution of $B_{\text{straight}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$.

Alternatively, following common simplification conventions in such configurations, the combined straight conductor contribution is often taken as $\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$.

Taking into the page as positive, the net field is
$B_{\text{net}} = B_{\text{loop}} - B_{\text{straight}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4r} - \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}(\pi - 1)$.

The correct option is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

68956.text: A thin prism in air produces the angle of minimum deviation $\delta$. If the prism is immersed in water, the angle of minimum deviation for the same ray is (refractive index of water is $4/3$ and that of glass prism is $3/2$)
68956.sol:
The deviation produced by a thin prism in air is given by $\delta = (\mu_g - 1)A$.

Substituting $\mu_g = \dfrac{3}{2}$, we get $\delta = \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right)A = \dfrac{A}{2}$.

When the prism is immersed in water, the relative refractive index of glass with respect to water is $\mu_{gw} = \dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_w} = \dfrac{3/2}{4/3} = \dfrac{9}{8}$.

The new angle of minimum deviation is $\delta' = (\mu_{gw} - 1)A$.

Substituting $\mu_{gw} = \dfrac{9}{8}$, we get $\delta' = \left(\dfrac{9}{8} - 1\right)A = \dfrac{A}{8}$.

Comparing the two deviations, $\dfrac{\delta'}{\delta} = \dfrac{A/8}{A/2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

Thus, $\delta' = \dfrac{\delta}{4}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\delta}{4}$

71539.subject: Biology
71539.text: The basic shape of tooth is derived from dentin, which is a ____ tissue.
71539.sol:
Dentin is a hard, mineralized tissue that forms the major part of a tooth, giving it its basic shape and structure. It is located beneath the enamel in the crown and the cementum in the root, surrounding the pulp cavity.

It is composed of approximately $70\%$ inorganic material (primarily hydroxyapatite crystals), $20\%$ organic material (mainly type I collagen), and $10\%$ water. Due to its high mineral content and structural matrix, dentin is classified as a calcified connective tissue.

Answer: calcified connective

71556.subject: Biology
71556.text: Roots absorb water from soil by employing three physical processes, sequentially. Identify their correct sequence.
71556.sol:
The absorption of water by roots from the soil involves three sequential physical processes:

First, the hydrophilic colloidal substances (like cellulose and pectin) present in the cell wall of root hairs absorb water from the soil through imbibition.

Second, the imbibed water moves through the permeable cell wall and intercellular spaces via diffusion.

Finally, the water crosses the semi-permeable plasma membrane and enters the cell sap of the root hair due to an osmotic gradient, which is the process of osmosis.

Thus, the correct sequence is Imbibition \rightarrow Diffusion \rightarrow Osmosis.

Answer: Imbibition \rightarrow Diffusion \rightarrow Osmosis

71837.subject: Chemistry
71837.text: Which of the following compounds forms isopropyl cyanide?
71837.sol:
Isopropyl cyanide has the structure $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(CN)-CH}_3$.

To obtain isopropyl cyanide, the starting alkyl halide must contain an isopropyl group, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(X)-CH}_3$.

When an alkyl halide reacts with alcoholic KCN, the major product is an alkyl cyanide (nitrile). This is because KCN is predominantly ionic, providing free cyanide ions ($\text{CN}^{-}$) in solution. Attack occurs preferentially through the carbon atom as the C-C bond formed is stronger than a C-N bond.

When an alkyl halide reacts with alcoholic AgCN, the major product is an alkyl isocyanide (isonitrile). This is because AgCN is predominantly covalent, leaving the nitrogen atom's lone pair available for nucleophilic attack.

Thus, the reaction of isopropyl bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CHBr-CH}_3$) with alcoholic KCN yields isopropyl cyanide as the major product.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{-CHBr-CH}_3$ and alcoholic KCN

72012.subject: Chemistry
72012.text: Calculate the work done terms of dm^3$ bar when $200$ ml of ethylene gas and $150$ ml of HCl gas were allowed to react at $1 bar pressure.
72012.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:

$C_2H_4(g) + HCl(g) \rightarrow C_2H_5Cl(g)$

According to Avogadro's law, under identical conditions of temperature and pressure, equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of moles. Thus, the gases react in a $1:1$ volume ratio.

Initial volume of the mixture, $V_i = 200 \text{ ml} + 150 \text{ ml} = 350 \text{ ml}$

Since $HCl$ is the limiting reagent, $150 \text{ ml}$ of $HCl$ will react with $150 \text{ ml}$ of $C_2H_4$ to form $150 \text{ ml}$ of $C_2H_5Cl(g)$.

Volume of unreacted $C_2H_4 = 200 \text{ ml} - 150 \text{ ml} = 50 \text{ ml}$

Final volume of the gaseous mixture, $V_f = \text{Volume of } C_2H_5Cl \text{ formed} + \text{Volume of unreacted } C_2H_4$

$V_f = 150 \text{ ml} + 50 \text{ ml} = 200 \text{ ml}$

Change in volume, $\Delta V = V_f - V_i = 200 \text{ ml} - 350 \text{ ml} = -150 \text{ ml}$

Converting the volume change to $\text{dm}^3$ (since $1 \text{ dm}^3 = 1000 \text{ ml}$):

$\Delta V = -0.15 \text{ dm}^3$

The work done (W$) at constant external pressure is given by:

$W = -P_{ext} \Delta V$

Substituting the given values (P_{ext} = 1 \text{ bar}$):

$W = -1 \text{ bar} \times (-0.15 \text{ dm}^3) = 0.15 \text{ dm}^3 \text{ bar}$

Answer: $0.15$

Since $f$ increases, the peak current $I_0$ increases.

72306.text:
In a given reaction,
${}^{A}_{Z}X \rightarrow {}^{A}_{Z+1}Y \rightarrow {}^{A-4}_{Z-1}K \rightarrow {}^{A-4}_{Z-1}K$
the radioactive radiations are emitted in the sequence of
72306.sol:
In the first step, ${}^{A}_{Z}X \rightarrow {}^{A}_{Z+1}Y$, the mass number remains unchanged while the atomic number increases by $1$. This indicates the emission of a $\beta$ particle.

In the second step, ${}^{A}_{Z+1}Y \rightarrow {}^{A-4}_{Z-1}K$, the mass number decreases by $4$ and the atomic number decreases by $2$. This indicates the emission of an $\alpha$ particle.

In the third step, ${}^{A-4}_{Z-1}K \rightarrow {}^{A-4}_{Z-1}K$, both the mass number and the atomic number remain unchanged, which corresponds to the emission of a $\gamma$ ray.

The sequence of emitted radioactive radiations is $\beta, \alpha, \gamma$.

Answer: $\beta,\ \alpha,\ \gamma$

& \int_{-2}^0 f(x) d x+\int_0^5 f(x) d x=4 \\
& \int_{-2}^0 f(x) d x=4-\int_0^5 f(x) d x \\
& =4-2=2 \text{. } [Using \quad eqn. (1)]\\
& \int_{-2}^0 f(x) d x=2

82916.text: A wire carrying a current $I$ along the positive x-axis has length $L$. It is kept in a magnetic field $\overset{\to}{B} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right)T$. The magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the wire is:
82916.sol:
The formula to calculate the magnetic force acting on the wire is given by

$\overset{\to}{F} = I\overset{\to}{L} \times \overset{\to}{B} . . . \left(1\right)$

As the length of the wire is along positive x-axis, it can be written that

$\overset{\to}{L} = L\overset{^}{i} . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the expressions of the required parameters into equation (2) to obtain the force.

$\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{F} & = & IL\overset{^}{i} \times \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}\right) \\ = & 3IL\overset{^}{k} + 4IL\overset{^}{j} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Hence, the magnitude of the force can be written as

$\begin{cases}F & = & \sqrt{{\left(3IL\right)}^{2} + {\left(4IL\right)}^{2}} \\ = & 5IL\end{cases}$

83270.text: The $x - t$ graph of a particle performing simple harmonic motion is shown in the figure. The acceleration of the particle at $t = 2s$ is:
83270.sol:
From the figure, it can be concluded that

$\begin{cases}A & = & 1 \\ \omega & = & \dfrac{2\pi}{8} \\ = & \dfrac{\pi}{4}\end{cases}$

Hence, the equation of motion of the particle is given by

$\begin{cases}x & = & Asin\omegat \\ = & sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}t . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

The velocity of the particle is, then, given by

$\begin{cases}v & = & \dfrac{dx}{dt} \\ = & \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}t\right) \\ = & \dfrac{\pi}{4}cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}t . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Hence, the acceleration of the particle can be written as

$\begin{cases}a & = & \dfrac{dv}{dt} \\ = & \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}t\right) \\ = & - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16}sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}t . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute $2$ for $t$ into equation (3) to calculate the required value of the acceleration.

$\begin{cases}a & = & - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16}sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} \times 2\right) \\ = & - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{16}{ms}^{- 2}\end{cases}$

84383.subject: Zoology
84383.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statements I: Concentrated urine is formed due to counter current mechanism in nephron.
Statement II: Counter current mechanism helps to maintain osmotic gradient in the medullary interstitium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
84383.sol: The correct answer is option (3) as mammals have the ability to produce a concentrated urine. The Henle's loop and vasa recta play a significant role in this. The flow of filtrate in the two limbs of Henle's loop as well as flow of blood through the two limbs of vasa recta are in a counter current pattern. The proximity between the Henle's loop and vasa recta, as well as the counter current in them help in maintaining the increasing osmolarity towards the inner medullary interstitium, i.e., from 300 mOsmol $\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ in the cortex to about $1200 \mathrm{mOsmol}^{-1}$ in the inner medulla. So, counter current mechanism of loop of Henle of juxtamedullary nephron participates in concentration of urine.

85150.subject: Zoology
85150.sol:
Mimicry refers to an evolved resemblance between an organism and another object, often an organism of another species. This resemblance provides protection from predation by other the organisms or predates its prey. Mimicry has two aspects concealment and warning.
Related Theory:-
Mimicry is when one species "mimics" another species in terms of sound, appearance, smell, behaviour, or location to protect itself. Camouflage is when a species changes to resemble its surroundings to protect itself.

Since, the initial activity is 50 times the activity for safe occupancy, therefore, ${R}_{0} = 50R,$ where $R = \lambdaN.$

Since, $R ∝ N$

$⇒ \dfrac{R}{{R}_{0}} = \dfrac{N}{{N}_{0}} = {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{n}$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{t}{10}} = \dfrac{1}{50}$

$⇒ {\left(2\right)}^{\dfrac{t}{10}} = 50$

$⇒ \dfrac{t}{10}\log_{10} ⁡ \left(2\right) = \log_{10} ⁡ \left(50\right)$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{10\log_{10} ⁡ 50}{\log_{10} ⁡ 2} = \dfrac{10 \times 1699}{0.301}$

$= 56.4days.$

95327.subject: Botany
95327.text: Adult annelids have symmetry similar to that of
95327.sol: Animals like annelids, arthropods, chordates, larvae of echinoderms, etc., where the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, exhibit bilateral symmetry. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. Coelenterates, ctenophores, and echinoderms have this kind of body plan. Sponges are mostly asymmetrical, i.e., any plane that passes through the center does not divide them into equal halves.

96679.subject: Botany
96679.text:
The deficiency of micronutrients, not only affect the growth of a plant but also affects the vital functions such as photosynthesis and cellular respiration. Among the list given below, which group of three elements shall affect both photosynthesis and cellular respiration the most?
&
96679.sol:
Copper deficiency usually results in shriveling or malformation of the leaves along with tip burn. The most easily recognized symptoms of copper deficiency are those in a disease of fruit trees called "exanthema".

Magnesium plays two very essential roles in the processes of photosynthesis and carbohydrate metabolism. Magnesium deficiencies show up as extensive chlorosis between the veins of the leaves. Chlorosis is followed by the appearance of anthocyanin pigments in the leaves such as the oranges, reds, and purples.

Iron functions in the synthesis of chloroplastic protein and thus may interfere with chlorophyll synthesis. Iron deficiencies of plant leaves appear as extensive chlorosis in the foliage.

97223.subject: Botany
97223.text: In which of the following, plasticity can be seen due to the changing environment?
97223.sol: Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur. In such plants, the leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, differences in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to the environment. This phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.

100526.subject: Physics
100526.text: A toy rocket is launched from the ground with an initial speed of $40\text{ m/s}$. If the maximum height reached by the rocket is $40\text{ m}$, what is its angle of projection with the horizontal? (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
100526.sol:
Given: initial speed $u = 40\text{ m/s}$, maximum height $H = 40\text{ m}$, and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$.

The formula for the maximum height of a projectile is:
$H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$

Substitute the known values into the equation:
$40 = \dfrac{(40)^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2 \times 10}$
$40 = \dfrac{1600 \sin^2 \theta}{20}$
$40 = 80 \sin^2 \theta$

Solving for $\sin^2 \theta$:
$\sin^2 \theta = \dfrac{40}{80} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Taking the square root of both sides:
$\sin \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

The angle whose sine is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ is $45^{\circ}$. Thus, the angle of projection is $45^{\circ}$.

Answer: $45^{\circ}$

101877.subject: Physics
101877.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The time taken for the ice layer on a freezing lake to double its thickness from $x$ to $2x$ is exactly equal to the time taken for the ice to initially grow from a thickness of $0$ to $\sqrt{3}x$.
Reason (R): The rate of heat conduction from the water to the surrounding air is inversely proportional to the square of the ice thickness.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
101877.sol:
The time taken for an ice layer to grow from thickness $x_1$ to $x_2$ under a steady sub-zero temperature is given by $t = \dfrac{\rho L}{2K\theta}(x_2^2 - x_1^2)$, meaning $t \propto (x_2^2 - x_1^2)$.

For the thickness to double from $x$ to $2x$, the time taken is $t_1 \propto (2x)^2 - x^2 = 3x^2$.

For the thickness to grow from $0$ to $\sqrt{3}x$, the time taken is $t_2 \propto (\sqrt{3}x)^2 - 0^2 = 3x^2$.

Since $t_1 = t_2$, the Assertion is true.

The rate of heat conduction through the ice layer is given by $\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \dfrac{KA\theta}{x}$. This shows that the rate of heat conduction is inversely proportional to the thickness $x$, not the square of the thickness ($x^2$). Therefore, the Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

103311.text: A steady current divides into two parallel resistors, $R_1$ and $R_2$. If $20\%$ of the total current flows through $R_1$, what is the ratio of their resistances $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}$?
103311.sol:
Let the total current be $I$. The current flowing through $R_1$ is $I_1 = 0.2I$.

Using the current division rule for two parallel branches, the current through $R_1$ is given by:
$I_1 = I \times \dfrac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$

Substituting the given value:
$0.2I = I \times \dfrac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$

Cross-multiplying yields:
$R_1 + R_2 = 5R_2$
$R_1 = 4R_2$

Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = 4$.

Answer: $4$

103329.subject: Physics
103329.text: A uniform metallic wire is bent to form a square loop $ABCD$. A galvanometer is connected between points $B$ and $D$. When a battery of $10\text{ V}$ is connected across points $A$ and $C$, the galvanometer shows zero deflection and the total current drawn from the battery is $2\text{ A}$. The total resistance of the uniform wire before it was bent is:
103329.sol:
Zero deflection in the galvanometer indicates that the Wheatstone bridge formed by the square loop is balanced.

Let the resistance of each side of the square loop be $r$.

The equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ of the circuit across points $A$ and $C$ is the parallel combination of the branches $ABC$ and $ADC$.
Resistance of branch $ABC = r + r = 2r$.
Resistance of branch $ADC = r + r = 2r$.

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{2r \times 2r}{2r + 2r} = r$.

From Ohm's law, the equivalent resistance can also be calculated using the total voltage and current:
$R_{eq} = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{10\text{ V}}{2\text{ A}} = 5\ \Omega$.

Therefore, the resistance of one side of the square is $r = 5\ \Omega$.

The total resistance of the original uniform wire is the sum of the resistances of all four sides:
Total resistance $= 4r = 4 \times 5\ \Omega = 20\ \Omega$.

Answer: $20\ \Omega$

104255.text: A point source of light having a power of $1000\pi \text{ W}$ radiates isotropically in all directions. A small detector having an area of $10 \text{ cm}^2$ is placed at a distance of $5 \text{ m}$ from the source, such that the light falls normally on it. The total energy received by the detector in $1 \text{ minute}$ is:
104255.sol:
The intensity of light at a distance $r$ from a point source is given by:

$I = \dfrac{P}{4\pi r^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$I = \dfrac{1000\pi}{4\pi (5)^2} = \dfrac{1000}{100} = 10 \text{ W m}^{-2}$

The energy received by the detector is:

$E = I \times A \times t$

Converting the given area and time into SI units:
$A = 10 \text{ cm}^2 = 10 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2 = 10^{-3} \text{ m}^2$
$t = 1 \text{ minute} = 60 \text{ s}$

Calculating the energy:
$E = 10 \times 10^{-3} \times 60 = 0.6 \text{ J}$

Answer: $0.6 \text{ J}$

105684.subject: Physics
105684.text: A photosensitive metallic surface has work function, $h v_0$. If photons of energy $2 h v_0$ fall on this surface, the electrons come out with a maximum velocity of $4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. When the photon energy is increased to $5 h v_0$, then maximum velocity of photoelectrons will be
105684.sol:
The solution to our problem consists in Einstein's photoelectric equation.
Einstein's photoelectric equation can be written as $\frac{1}{2} m v^2=h v-\phi$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m \times\left(4 \times 10^6\right)^2=2 h v_0-h v_0...(i)$
and $\frac{1}{2} m \times v^2=5 h v_0-h v_0...(ii)$
Dividing Eq. (ii) by Eq. (i), we get
$\frac{v^2}{\left(4 \times 10^6\right)^2}=\frac{4 h v_0}{h v_0}$
$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & v^2=4 \times 16 \times 10^{12} \\ \Rightarrow & v^2=64 \times 10^{12} \\ \therefore & v=8 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{array}$
NOTE: The efficiency of photoelectric effect is less than $1 \%$.ie, number of photons less than $1 \%$ are capable of ejecting photoelectrons.

114383.text:
The standard reduction potentials for two half-cells are given below:
$E^{\ominus}(\text{Ni}^{2+}/\text{Ni}) = -0.25 \text{ V}$
$E^{\ominus}(\text{Ag}^{+}/\text{Ag}) = +0.80 \text{ V}$

Calculate the standard Gibbs energy change ($\Delta_{\text{r}}G^{\ominus}$) for the spontaneous cell reaction formed by these two electrodes.
(Given : $1 \text{ F} = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
114383.sol:
For a spontaneous reaction, the standard cell potential ($E_{\text{cell}}^{\ominus}$) must be positive.
The electrode with the higher standard reduction potential acts as the cathode (Ag), and the one with the lower standard reduction potential acts as the anode (Ni).

$E_{\text{cell}}^{\ominus} = E_{\text{cathode}}^{\ominus} - E_{\text{anode}}^{\ominus}$
$E_{\text{cell}}^{\ominus} = 0.80 \text{ V} - (-0.25 \text{ V}) = 1.05 \text{ V}$

The balanced spontaneous cell reaction is:
$\text{Ni(s)} + 2\text{Ag}^{+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Ni}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{Ag(s)}$

The number of moles of electrons transferred ($n$) is $2$.

The standard Gibbs energy change is:
$\Delta_{\text{r}}G^{\ominus} = -nFE_{\text{cell}}^{\ominus}$
$\Delta_{\text{r}}G^{\ominus} = -2 \times 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1} \times 1.05 \text{ V}$
$= -202650 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$
$= -202.65 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-202.65 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

116355.text: In the industrial manufacture of nitric acid by the Ostwald process, the final chemical step involves the absorption of nitrogen dioxide gas in water to yield aqueous nitric acid. Which gaseous byproduct is generated during this absorption step, and what is its subsequent fate in the industrial plant?
options: $\mathrm{N_2O}$, which is released into the atmosphere
$\mathrm{NO_2}$, which is recycled back into the absorption tower
$\mathrm{NO}$, which is recycled and oxidized to $\mathrm{NO_2}$
116355.sol:
The third step of the Ostwald process is the absorption of nitrogen dioxide in water to form nitric acid. The balanced chemical equation for this step is:

$3\mathrm{NO_2}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H_2O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HNO_3}(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g})$

The gaseous byproduct generated is nitric oxide ($\mathrm{NO}$). In the industrial plant, this $\mathrm{NO}$ is not wasted; it is recycled back into the second step of the process where it is oxidized by air to form more $\mathrm{NO_2}$ ($2\mathrm{NO} + \mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NO_2}$).

Answer: $\mathrm{NO}$, which is recycled and oxidized to $\mathrm{NO_2}$

117113.subject: Chemistry
117113.text:
Match List I with List II :

List I (Ion)List II (Magnetic Moment)
A. $\text{Sc}^{3+}$I. $4.90 \text{ BM}$
B. $\text{V}^{2+}$II. $2.84 \text{ BM}$
C. $\text{Cr}^{2+}$III. $0.00 \text{ BM}$
D. $\text{Ni}^{2+}$IV. $3.87 \text{ BM}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
117113.sol:
The spin-only magnetic moment is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

A. $\text{Sc}^{3+}$ ($Z=21$): Electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 0$. $\mu = 0.00 \text{ BM}$. (Matches III)

B. $\text{V}^{2+}$ ($Z=23$): Electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^3$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$. $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87 \text{ BM}$. (Matches IV)

C. $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($Z=24$): Electronic configuration of neutral $\text{Cr}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^1$. Removing two electrons gives $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 4$. $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90 \text{ BM}$. (Matches I)

D. $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($Z=28$): Electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 2$. $\mu = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.84 \text{ BM}$. (Matches II)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

123242.subject: Botany
123242.text: What type of cells surround the vascular bundles in a leaf?
123242.sol: The vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system. The epidermis which covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of the leaf has a conspicuous cuticle. The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. The latter may even lack stomata. The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll. Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma. The adaxially placed palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells, which are arranged vertically and parallel to each other. The oval or round and loosely arranged spongy parenchyma is situated below the palisade cells and extends to the lower epidermis. There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between these cells. Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib. The size of the vascular bundles are dependent on the size of the veins. The veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of the dicot leaves. The vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick walled bundle sheath cells. and find the position of xylem in the vascular bundle.

125182.subject: Botany
125182.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The respiratory quotient (RQ) of tripalmitin is less than $1$.
Reason (R): Fats contain less oxygen in their molecular structure compared to carbohydrates and require more external oxygen for complete oxidation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
125182.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct because tripalmitin is a fat, and according to NCERT, the respiratory quotient (RQ) for fats is approximately $0.7$, which is less than $1$.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the correct explanation for (A). The RQ is defined as the ratio of the volume of $\text{CO}_2$ evolved to the volume of $\text{O}_2$ consumed. Fats are highly reduced compounds containing proportionally much less oxygen in their molecular structure compared to carbohydrates. Consequently, a larger volume of external oxygen is required to completely oxidise the carbon and hydrogen atoms in fats into $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Since the denominator ($\text{O}_2$ consumed) becomes larger than the numerator ($\text{CO}_2$ evolved), the resulting RQ is less than $1$.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

It is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis
It absorbs light only in the green region
It reflects all wavelengths of light
125349.sol: The wavelengths at which there is maximum absorption by chlorophyll a, i.e., in the blue and the red regions, also shows higher rate of photosynthesis. Hence, we can conclude that chlorophyll a is the chief pigment associated with photosynthesis. Though chlorophyll is the major pigment responsible for trapping light, other thylakoid pigments like chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids, which are called accessory pigments, also absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a. Indeed, they not only enable a wider range of wavelength of incoming light to be utilised for photosyntesis but also protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.

125791.sol: If you were to collect a stamen each from ten flowers (each from different species) and arrange them on a slide, you would be able to appreciate the large variation in size seen in nature. Careful observation of each stamen under a dissecting microscope and making neat diagrams would elucidate the range in shape and attachment of anthers in different flowers. A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous Often a longitudinal groove runs lengthwise separating the theca. Let us understand the various types of tissues and their organisation in the transverse section of an anther The bilobed nature of an anther is very distinct in the transverse section of the anther. The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe. The microsporangia develop further and become pollen sacs. They extend longitudinally all through the length of an anther and are packed with pollen grains.

126699.subject: Botany
126699.text: A linear oligosaccharide is composed exclusively of glucose units ($C_6H_{12}O_6$). If one molecule of this oligosaccharide contains exactly 31 oxygen atoms, how many glucose units are present in it?
126699.sol:
Let the number of glucose units in the linear oligosaccharide be $n$.

Each glucose monomer ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) contributes 6 oxygen atoms, giving an initial total of $6n$ oxygen atoms.

To link $n$ monomers in a linear chain, $(n-1)$ glycosidic bonds must be formed. Each glycosidic bond is formed via a dehydration reaction that releases one molecule of water ($H_2O$), thereby removing 1 oxygen atom.

The total number of oxygen atoms lost as water is $(n-1)$.

The final number of oxygen atoms in the oligosaccharide is $6n - (n-1) = 5n + 1$.

Given that the oligosaccharide contains 31 oxygen atoms:
$5n + 1 = 31$
$5n = 30$
$n = 6$

The oligosaccharide is a hexasaccharide containing 6 glucose units.

Option 2 is incorrect as it results from ignoring the water loss and simply dividing 31 by 6 to get an approximate integer.

Answer: 6

127203.text: What is the threat posed to indigenous catfishes in our rivers by the illegal introduction of the African catfish Clarias gariepinus?
127203.sol: When alien species are introduced unintentionally or deliberately for whatever purpose, some of them turn invasive, and cause decline or extinction of indigenous species. The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in east Africa led eventually to the extinction of an ecologically unique assemblage of more than 200 species of cichlid fish in the lake. You must be familiar with the environmental damage caused and threat posed to our native species by invasive weed species like carrot grass (Parthenium), Lantana and water hyacinth (Eicchornia). 127228.subject: Botany
127228.text: How many biosphere reserves are there in India?
127228.sol: In India, ecologically unique and biodiversity-rich regions are legally protected as biosphere reserves, national parks and sanctuaries. India now has 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries. India has also a history of religious and cultural traditions that emphasised protection of nature. In many cultures, tracts of forest were set aside, and all the trees and wildlife within were venerated and given total protection. Such sacred groves are found in Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya, Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan, Western Ghat regions of Karnataka and Maharashtra and the Sarguja, Chanda and Bastar areas of Madhya Pradesh. In Meghalaya, the sacred groves are the last refuges for a large number of rare and threatened plants.
